chunks: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a man who has a right against another man, but he denies his right and swears that he owes him nothing. The owner of the right has no proof for his right. Is it permissible for him to recover his right through false testimony if he fears the loss of his right?
He عليه السلام said: “That is not permissible, due to the cause of deception.”

key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal proof or evidentiary support for a claim
key_terms.حَقٌّ: a due right or claim owed to someone
key_terms.ذَهَابَ حَقِّهِ: the loss or disappearance of one’s rightful claim
key_terms.شَهَادَةِ الزُّورِ: false testimony given contrary to the truth

ai.seo_question: Can someone recover a denied right through false testimony if they fear losing it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a person may not use false testimony to reclaim a right, even if the other party denies it and no evidence is available. The Imam عليه السلام forbids this because it involves deception, showing that unlawful means cannot be used to secure a lawful claim.
